doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Father as teacher: home schooling, expulsion from Virginia, and his death
summary: His father taught the children, was run out of a Virginia town, read to them nightly, worked several jobs and died at 72.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You’re doing this as you’re a young man. Would you consider yourself – how did you achieve an education?

A lot of the times, whenever we weren’t able to stay in one place and go to school, my dad was teaching us anyway, because he taught school. He actually taught public school. He was teaching in the South. He was teaching in the white school, but he reprimanded the mayor’s son once, and they ran us out of town.
That was in Virginia. But he was a very smart man.

So, at some point after Jeannette and your families travels, you ended up living back in Virginia, where the family had originated? Or did this expulsion from Virginia, did that lead him to Pennsylvania?

That’s the part of what led to Pennsylvania, that expulsion. No, we never went back there. I don’t think that would have been wise. Though we did most of our – the kids started to go to school in Indianapolis. My dad was still always teaching us anyway. He was – every night he would get us together and read to us.
What would he read to you?

Different kinds of stories. He’d just read to us every night, the whole family. During the day we’d be rehearsing. We’d be practicing. It was always music in that house. My mother was like the mother of the whole block. If you didn’t have any food, you could come to our house. We were poor, but there was always food there, because my dad always worked. He worked several jobs at the same time.
Even as he had the family band.
Whenever he was with the family band, he still was working jobs. He was a guy that would get up in the morning and start doing something – every morning.
How long did your dad live?
He only lived until 72. It probably was maybe just a fluke that he died at that age, because it probably was a heart attack, which could have been stopped by an aspirin, but we didn’t know.
